title: Bhutan glacial lake burst: Sankosh surge passes north Bengal without major flooding
dek: About 12,000 people were moved from the Sankosh banks in Alipurduar as the river rose on Friday. Officials say the situation is under control and no casualties have been reported in Bengal or Assam.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
About 12,000 people have been moved away from the banks of the Sankosh river in north Bengal's Alipurduar district after a glacial lake burst in Bhutan sent a surge of water downstream, officials said on Friday, October 30. The river had risen by nearly two feet since Friday morning, a senior official told news agency PTI, and a red alert remains in force for the Sankosh system.

No deaths or major damage have been reported in Bengal. "The situation is under control at present," the official said.

By Friday evening the surge had largely passed through the Sankosh in Alipurduar and Cooch Behar districts without major flooding, news agency UNI reported from Siliguri, and some families from forest villages who had spent Thursday night in schools and shelters had gone home. A senior state official told NEnow on Friday evening that conditions remained under control. No report of the red alert being withdrawn had been issued by the time of writing.

## What happened in Bhutan

The Shintaphu glacial lake in Bhutan's Gasa district burst its banks on Thursday evening, October 29, releasing an estimated 7.4 million cubic metres of water, mud, rocks and debris into the Mo Chhu river system, according to reports. The Mo Chhu feeds the Punatsangchhu, which becomes the Sankosh as it flows into India along the border between West Bengal and Assam. Shintaphu is on Bhutan's official list of potentially dangerous glacial lakes.

In Bhutan, the flood washed away a stretch of the Punakha-Gasa road and damaged the area around the Gasa Tshachu hot springs, Open magazine and IANS reported. No deaths or injuries had been reported there as of Friday morning.

## In Alipurduar

The Central Water Commission had warned on Thursday night of a sudden rise in water levels in Alipurduar and in Dhubri in Assam. Alipurduar Superintendent of Police Amit Kumar Shaw said 4,000 to 5,000 people were in shelters, mostly school buildings, and more than 6,000 others had been moved to safer places, with dry food and drinking water arranged. He said there was "absolutely no need to panic". Reports differ slightly on the total: PTI, citing a senior official, put it at 12,000.

The river looked calm on Friday morning and some families in Kumargram block went home, IANS reported, but the water rose sharply in several stretches in the afternoon and turned muddy, and many returned to the relief camps. Some spent Thursday night on the national highway.

State minister Nisith Pramanik said residents along the Sankosh and its tributaries had been alerted and that floodwater was expected to reach the plains within five to six hours, IANS reported; the time of his remarks was not given. National Disaster Response Force personnel have been deployed, along with State Disaster Response Force and Civil Defence teams, officials said. Authorities have warned that debris, including large pieces of wood and concrete, could come down the river.

## Assam and the weather

In Assam, the state disaster management authority said on Friday that no evacuations had been needed in Dhubri and that river levels had not risen so far. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said teams were on standby in Dhubri and Kokrajhar. On Friday evening, Dhubri Deputy Commissioner Dibakar Nath said the district was on high alert and monitoring the situation closely, and urged people not to panic or let family members bathe in the river. The Assam Tribune reported no abnormal rise in the Sankosh or Gangadhar rivers in the district, and The Pioneer, citing the Chief Minister's office, said levels in Dhubri and Kokrajhar remained steady.

In Jalpaiguri district, an official told The Pioneer the burst had no effect on rivers there, though precautionary announcements were made in Banarhat, Binnaguri and Nagrakata.

The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rain in Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Jalpaiguri and Alipurduar until Saturday morning as the remnants of Cyclone Arnab move north.

Evacuation figures have differed between officials and outlets through the day, from several thousand to about 12,000. This is a developing story and figures may change.
